label: survey:languages
method: Shallow git clones under $S/survey/src; sizes measured with $S/tools/measure.sh (Cortex-M4, -Os) – commands in $S/engines/survey-refs/BUILD.txt, $S/engines/duktape/BUILD.txt, $S/engines/jerryscript/BUILD.txt. Quotes come from files read in the clones or pages fetched (gh CLI / WebFetch).

languages.name: MicroPython (re, formerly ure)
languages.regex_support: third-party(re1.5, pfalcon, bytecode + recursive backtracking, ~530 lines)
languages.algorithm: compile to bytecode, recursive backtracking matcher (recursiveloop.c)
languages.features: docs/library/re.rst: . [] ^ $ ? * + ?? *? +? | (...) (?:...) \d\D\s\S\w\W; NOT: {m,n}, named groups, \b \B, \r \n escapes. UTF-8 aware only when MICROPY_PY_BUILTINS_STR_UNICODE (modre.c:36,128).
languages.size_evidence: measured: re1.5 engine 1566 B text (compilecode 1080 + recursiveloop 336 + charclass 150), Cortex-M4 -Os; $S/engines/survey-refs/BUILD.txt
languages.size_was_reason: py/mpconfig.h:2003 '#define MICROPY_PY_RE (MICROPY_CONFIG_ROM_LEVEL_AT_LEAST_EXTRA_FEATURES)' and :88-91 BASIC_FEATURES='small on-device flash, e.g. STM32F411', EXTRA_FEATURES='medium on-device flash' -> re is off on MINIMUM/CORE/BASIC ports (ports/nrf/mpconfigport.h:33-45 nRF51822+SoftDevice=MINIMUM, nRF52832=BASIC). pfalcon in issue #3403 (https://github.com/micropython/micropython/issues/3403): 'ure's idea is to be minimal' and re-pcre 'there're no immediate size constraints there'. re1.5 README (https://github.com/pfalcon/re1.5): 'sticking to the minimal code size and memory use', 'intended for use in highly constrained, e.g. embedded, environments'.
languages.notes: samd21 explicitly re-enables it (ports/samd/mcu/samd21/mpconfigmcu.h:31) on a BASIC_FEATURES build -> maintainers consider it cheap enough for 256 kB parts.

languages.name: CircuitPython
languages.features: same subset as MicroPython
languages.size_evidence: same engine (1566 B)
languages.size_was_reason: py/circuitpy_mpconfig.mk:512 'CIRCUITPY_RE ?= $(CIRCUITPY_FULL_BUILD)'; :55-56 'Smaller builds can be forced for resource constrained chips (typically SAMD21s without external flash) by setting CIRCUITPY_FULL_BUILD=0'. ports/atmel-samd/mpconfigport.mk:24-49: 'Some of these are on by default with CIRCUITPY_FULL_BUILD, but don't fit in 256kB of flash' ... 'CIRCUITPY_RE ?= 0'. ports/stm/boards/blues_cygnet/mpconfigboard.mk:67 'CIRCUITPY_RE = 0' (STM32L433, FULL_BUILD=0). 55 boards set CIRCUITPY_FULL_BUILD=0, 75 samd21 boards -> re dropped for flash.
languages.notes: Strong evidence: re is one of the first modules cut on 256 kB parts, alongside json, msgpack, aesio.

languages.name: Berry (core) / Berry in Tasmota
languages.regex_support: core: none; Tasmota adds third-party(re1.5) module 're'
languages.engine: be_re_lib.c ('Regex using re1.5', #include ../../re1.5/re1.5.h) + Tasmota copy of re1.5 in lib/libesp32/re1.5
languages.features: re1.5 subset (no {n,m}, no \b); Tasmota copy adds only TASMOTA-specific dumpcode/util tweaks (diff vs MicroPython copy is cosmetic)
languages.size_evidence: measured Tasmota re1.5 copy: 1102+336+126 = 1564 B text, Cortex-M4 -Os
languages.size_was_reason: no evidence (berry-lang/berry src has no regex at all; Tasmota chose the ~1.5 kB re1.5)
languages.notes: berry-lang/berry clone: grep for re1.5/regex in src/ and default/berry_conf.h -> nothing.

languages.name: Espruino
languages.engine: src/jswrap_regexp.c (476 lines, matchhere/matchcharacter recursive matcher, Kernighan/Pike style)
languages.algorithm: recursive backtracking directly on the pattern string (no compile step)
languages.features: jswrap_regexp.c:277-281: 'does not contain all the features present in a full ES6 JS engine ... not implemented: Assertions other than ^ and $; Numeric quantifiers (eg x{3})'; issue #1257 lists missing backreferences, x{3}, \b/\B, lookahead. Has classes, \d\w\s, * + ?, |, groups, i/g flags, lazy? (not documented).
languages.size_evidence: measured jswrap_regexp.c alone: 2267 B text (Cortex-M4 -Os, LINUX platform config); $S/engines/survey-refs/BUILD.txt
languages.size_was_reason: src/jsutils.h:41-58 '#ifdef SAVE_ON_FLASH ... #define ESPR_NO_REGEX 1 ... #define ESPR_NO_REGEX_OPTIMISE 1'; src/jsparse.c:1826-1827 '#ifdef ESPR_NO_REGEX jsExceptionHere(JSET_SYNTAXERROR, "RegEx not supported in this build")'; 15 of 71 boards/*.py set SAVE_ON_FLASH (BANGLEJS, ESPRUINOBOARD, MICROBIT1/2, NRF51822DK, NUCLEOF401RE/F411RE, PICO_R1_3, PIXLJS, STM32VLDISCOVERY ...); boards/PICO_R1_3.py:51 '-DESPR_NO_REGEX_OPTIMISE=1  # strip out regex optimisations to free some flash space'; ESP8266_BOARD/MDBT42Q/PIXLJS: 'ESPR_NO_REGEX_OPTIMISE  # save some storage space'. Release 1v95 (https://github.com/orgs/espruino/discussions/149): RegExp 'on all official Espruino boards (and many others, if there's enough memory)'. Gordon Williams (https://github.com/orgs/espruino/discussions/166): 'I'm sure it'll make the builds for the original Espruino a little more painful, but it's worth it - and not actually that much more code (it's not a 100% full-featured regex, but should be enough for basic stuff)'.
languages.notes: Clear case of regex being compiled out for flash on small boards, AND the author judging the engine 'not that much more code' (~2.3 kB).

languages.name: Duktape
languages.algorithm: doc/regexp.rst: compiles to PC-relative bytecode, 'recursive back-tracking matcher which uses the C stack whenever recursion is needed, but explicitly avoids doing so for simple quantifiers'; design priorities 'ECMAScript compatibility' and 'compactness'
languages.features: full ES5 RegExp incl. backrefs, lookahead, {n,m}, lazy, i/g/m; case-insensitive uses Unicode canonicalization (DUK_USE_REGEXP_CANON_BITMAP ~300-400 B, optional 128 kB workaround table)
languages.size_evidence: measured (duktape-2.7.0 src-separate, Cortex-M4 -Os): compiler 2786 + executor 2011 + RegExp builtin 794 = 5591 B, plus duk_unicode_re_* helpers ~250 B and re_canon_bitmap 256 B (~6.1 kB total); $S/engines/duktape/BUILD.txt. Whole engine ~200 kB (low-memory.rst: 'Duktape compiles to around 200-210kB of code (x86)').
languages.size_was_reason: Option DUK_USE_REGEXP_SUPPORT is tagged 'lowmemory' (config/config-options/DUK_USE_REGEXP_SUPPORT.yaml, 'Enable support for regular expressions (recommended)'); doc/low-memory.rst: 'If you don't need regexp support, use: #undef DUK_USE_REGEXP_SUPPORT'. No kB figure for regexp is documented.
languages.notes: Full ES5 regexp in ~6 kB shows a complete backtracking engine need not be large; the 200 kB core dwarfs it.

languages.name: QuickJS
languages.algorithm: bytecode compiler + backtracking executor with explicit stack (lre_exec)
languages.features: full ES2020+ RegExp (unicode, named groups, lookbehind, properties \p{..})
languages.size_evidence: measured: libregexp.c 13334 B text; libunicode.c 49046 B (tables, shared with String) – Cortex-M4 -Os
languages.size_was_reason: no evidence (always compiled in)
languages.notes: Shows where the bytes go: Unicode tables (49 kB) are 3.7x the matcher.

languages.name: MicroQuickJS (mquickjs, Bellard 2025)
languages.engine: regexp code inlined in mquickjs.c (lre_exec, re_parse_alternative, ...)
languages.features: README: 'Regexp: case folding only works with ASCII characters; the matching is unicode only i.e. /./ matches a unicode code point'; flags s,y,u accepted, no unicode properties. Otherwise full ES5 (backrefs, lookahead, {n,m}, lazy).
languages.size_evidence: measured: whole mquickjs.c 68089 B text (Cortex-M4 -Os); regexp core (lre_*/re_* functions+rodata) 6480 B + js_regexp* builtins 905 B = 7385 B (10.8%). README: 'The whole engine requires about 100 kB of ROM (ARM Thumb-2 code) including the C library'.
languages.size_was_reason: no evidence – regexp kept in a 100 kB engine, only Unicode case folding/properties dropped
languages.notes: Best modern reference point: full JS regexp semantics with UTF-8/code-point matching and ASCII-only folding in ~7.4 kB.

languages.name: JerryScript
languages.features: ES5.1/ES.next RegExp (backrefs, lookahead, {n,m}, lazy, named groups, u flag)
languages.size_evidence: measured cross-build (Cortex-M4 MinSizeRel, no LTO): regexp objects 13873 B of 253707 B jerry-core text (re-parser 3042, re-compiler 312, re-bytecode 432, ecma-regexp-object 7996, builtins 2091); $S/engines/jerryscript/BUILD.txt
languages.size_was_reason: docs list JERRY_BUILTIN_REGEXP / JERRY_REGEXP_STRICT_MODE options but no size figures (01.CONFIGURATION.md, profiles/README.md fetched). Building master with -DJERRY_BUILTIN_REGEXP=0 currently FAILS (ecma-builtin-regexp-string-iterator-prototype.c:168) -> nobody ships it disabled.
languages.notes: ~5.5% of the engine; the 'minimal' profile disables ES.next builtins, not RegExp specifically (unverified which profile disables it).

languages.name: mJS (Cesanta)
languages.features: README: 'No standard library. No String, Number, RegExp, Date, Function, etc.'
languages.size_evidence: README: 'On 32-bit ARM mJS engine takes about 50k of flash memory, and less than 1k of RAM'
languages.size_was_reason: no explicit regex-size quote; RegExp dropped together with the whole stdlib for a 50 kB engine

languages.name: Elk (Cesanta)
languages.features: README 'Not supported features': 'No standard library: no Date, Regexp, Function, String, Number'
languages.size_evidence: none
languages.size_was_reason: no evidence beyond minimalism (whole stdlib absent)

languages.name: V7 (Cesanta, predecessor)
languages.regex_support: own-engine (optional; source no longer in repo)
languages.features: ES5 RegExp
languages.size_evidence: README: 'Compiled static size is in 40k - 120k range'
languages.size_was_reason: features.md: '-DV7_BUILD_PROFILE=1 - Build minimal configuration: disable Date, UTF8, RegExp' -> RegExp is the first thing cut in the minimal profile
languages.notes: cesanta/slre (used by Mongoose) measured: 1946 B text, Cortex-M4 -Os.

languages.name: Lua (stock) / NodeMCU / eLua / MicroLua
languages.features: Lua patterns: classes %d %a %s.., sets, * + - ? (lazy '-'), captures, %b, %f, anchors; no alternation, no {n,m}, no UTF-8 classes
languages.size_evidence: measured lstrlib.c whole 9731 B (Cortex-M4 -Os); pattern-matching functions + their rodata ~2995 B
languages.size_was_reason: PiL 20.1: 'The main reason for this is size: A typical implementation of POSIX regexp takes more than 4,000 lines of code. This is bigger than all Lua standard libraries together. In comparison, the implementation of pattern matching in Lua has less than 500 lines.'
languages.notes: NodeMCU (app/lua/lstrlib.c, app/lua53/lstrlib.c), eLua (src/lua/lstrlib.c) and MicroLua (core/CMakeLists.txt:40 mlua_add_core_c_module(string lstrlib.c)) all inherit patterns unchanged; no regex added.

languages.name: Squirrel
languages.algorithm: compile to node list, recursive backtracking
languages.features: doc/source/stdlib/stdstringlib.rst: \ ^ . $ | (subexp) (?:subexp) [] greedy * + ? {n} {n,} {n,m}, classes \w\W\s\S\d\D\x\X\c\C\p\P\l\u\a\A; no lazy quantifiers, no case-insensitive flag, byte-wise
languages.size_evidence: measured sqstdrex.cpp: 3144 B text (Cortex-M4 -Os)
languages.size_was_reason: no evidence

languages.name: Wren
languages.size_evidence: none
languages.size_was_reason: issue #120 (2015, edsrzf): 'Regular expressions are probably out, since they'd either require a dependency or a complicated implementation.' munificent: 'I do worry it would add a lot of code to Wren, but maybe it won't be too bad.' Issue #933 (2021) still open; #1081 closed.
languages.notes: Explicit code-size/complexity worry from the language author.

languages.name: Janet
languages.features: PEG superset of regex
languages.size_evidence: measured peg.c: 12541 B text + 48 data (Cortex-M4 -Os)
languages.size_was_reason: no – docs: 'Janet has no built-in regex module because PEGs offer a superset of the functionality of regular expressions.'

languages.name: AtomVM (Erlang/Elixir on MCU)
languages.size_evidence: issue quotes tiny-regex-c: 'text 2404 ... re.o' as attractive
languages.size_was_reason: Mixed: UncleGrumpy: tiny-regex-c 'looks perfect for microcontrollers ... attractive on any constrained environment'; bettio rejects it: 'doesn't seem to support utf8, and we do use utf8' and prefers pure Erlang NFA 'in a reasonable amount of code'; petermm: 'support a substantial part of PCRE2 on top of some minimal regex lib like tiny-regex-c, for a few kBs'. libs/estdlib/src has no re module (clone).
languages.notes: Size is discussed but UTF-8 support is the actual blocker – matches this project's requirement list.

languages.name: Rust no_std (regex-lite)
languages.features: docs.rs: 'Perl character classes are limited to ASCII codepoints', no \p{..}, &str only, no RegexSet
languages.size_evidence: README: 'regex-lite 0.1.0: 0.73s compile time, 94KB relative size increase' vs 'regex 1.9.0: 1.93s compile time, 565KB relative size increase' (x86-64 binary)
languages.size_was_reason: README: 'The primary purpose of this crate is to provide an alternative regex engine for folks that are unhappy with the binary size and compilation time of the primary regex crate.'
languages.notes: Still ~94 kB – an order of magnitude above the C engines above; needs alloc.

languages.name: mruby
languages.regex_support: core: none; optional-module (mruby-regexp-pcre bundles PCRE; mruby-onig-regexp bundles Onigmo)

languages.size_evidence: none measured; gems are thin bindings (mruby_regexp_pcre.c 369 lines, mruby_onig_regexp.c 1386 lines) over multi-hundred-kB libraries
languages.size_was_reason: language.md:187: 'Regular expressions require an external gem such as mruby-regexp-pcre or mruby-onig-regexp. Without a regexp gem, Regexp literals (/pattern/) are not available.' – reason not stated (unverified).

languages.name: reference engines: tiny-regex-c, slre, re1.5, T-Rex, Jim, Espruino, Duktape, mquickjs, Janet PEG, QuickJS
languages.features: tiny-regex-c: no groups/alternation/UTF-8; slre: groups, no lazy, byte-wise; re1.5: no {n,m}; T-Rex: no lazy; mquickjs/Duktape/Jim: full
languages.size_evidence: Cortex-M4 -Os text bytes: tiny-regex-c 1532; re1.5 1566; slre 1946; Espruino 2267; Lua patterns ~2995; T-Rex 3144; Jim 5166; Duktape ~5591-6100; mquickjs 7385; QuickJS 13334 (+49046 unicode); Jerry 13873; Janet PEG 12541
languages.size_was_reason: n/a
languages.notes: All measured in this survey with the shared protocol.

verdict: Partly true, but mostly as a *historical/perceived* reason, not a measured one. FOR: Lua's documented rationale is explicitly size ('POSIX regexp takes more than 4,000 lines ... bigger than all Lua standard libraries', PiL 20.1); Wren's author feared it 'would add a lot of code'; Espruino compiles RegExp out under SAVE_ON_FLASH on 15/71 boards and strips its 'regex optimisations' to 'free some flash space'; CircuitPython turns CIRCUITPY_RE off on every SAMD21 because those modules 'don't fit in 256kB of flash'; MicroPython gates re behind the EXTRA_FEATURES ROM level; Duktape tags the option 'lowmemory'; V7's minimal profile drops RegExp first; Rust's regex-lite exists only because the main crate adds 565 kB. AGAINST: the engines these systems actually ship are small — re1.5 1.6 kB, Espruino 2.3 kB, slre 1.9 kB, T-Rex 3.1 kB, Jim 5.2 kB, Duktape ~6 kB and mquickjs ~7.4 kB for FULL JS semantics with code-point matching and ASCII folding (measured, Cortex-M4 -Os) — 1-3% of their hosts (Duktape ~200 kB, mquickjs 68-100 kB, Jerry 254 kB). The big numbers come from Unicode tables (QuickJS libunicode 49 kB) or desktop libraries (PCRE/Onigmo for mruby, Go regexp for TinyGo, 94 kB regex-lite). Where languages lack regex, the stated reasons are usually minimalism of the whole stdlib (mJS, Elk, uLisp, PicoC), a deliberate alternative (Janet PEG, Lua patterns), or a feature gap in the tiny candidates (AtomVM rejected tiny-regex-c for lacking UTF-8). Conclusion: the perception that regex is big is real and still shapes decisions, but no small runtime has published a measurement showing a modern-basics engine costs more than a few kB; the actual gap in the ecosystem is a ~1.5-2 kB engine with {n,m}, lazy quantifiers, UTF-8 code points and an ASCII i-flag — re1.5 (the most-copied one) lacks the first three.
